subject: Japanese spider crab
title: A Crab With 12-Foot Legs Has a Body the Size of a Large Pizza

scenes.text: This crab's legs reach twelve feet. Its body is pizza-sized.
The Japanese spider crab. Claw to claw, up to twelve and a half feet. The widest reach of any animal with a shell.
Yet the shell itself is only 16 inches across. Everything else is leg.
It weighs up to 42 pounds and lives on the dark seafloor off Japan, down to 1,900 feet, picking at dead fish.
Young ones glue sponges onto their shells as camouflage. Adults stop bothering. Almost nothing down there can eat them.
To grow, it climbs out of its own shell, legs and all, in about 100 minutes. Up to a hundred years of that.

description:
The Japanese spider crab has the widest leg span of any arthropod: up to 12.5 feet claw to claw, on a body only about 16 inches across.
It weighs up to 42 pounds, lives 160 to 1,900 feet down on the Pacific side of Japan, scavenges dead animals and pries open shells, and molts its whole shell, legs included, in roughly 100 minutes. It may live up to 100 years.
Would you dare to hold one? Comment below.
first_comment: Its Japanese name, taka-ashi-gani, means tall-legged crab. The first molt happens just 9 to 12 days after hatching. Which giant animal should we cover next?
